quest.title: A Proposition Beyond Refutation
quest.description: Inside the witch's dictionary, you discover a rather infantile "declaration of war"...
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Resistance x3, Mora x30000

chapter.title: Witch's Homework: Of What Is Contested

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Prune's assignment doesn't look much like homework... More like a declaration of war...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Hehehe, little Witch Hunter, have you found a way to defeat me yet? Shout your coolest challenge from the rooftops and prepare to bow down before the Dodo-King!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Paimon'll bet a million Mora that Alice wrote this. If it wasn't for the part about a "Witch Hunter," Paimon would've thought this was written for Klee.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Prune isn't exactly Alice's biggest fan... Paimon can see her really blowing her top over a challenge like this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alice clearly knows what she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we try to... tone things down a bit when we tell Prune?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Tell me what? Lemme see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Don't sneak up on Paimon like that! Fine... but you've gotta promise to keep it cool, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Ugh... Booooring.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're not mad?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Heh. I'm used to her childish little games. She likes to act mysterious, but it's all just cheap tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Who "shouts a challenge from the rooftops" anyway? People walking past would look at me like I'm crazy. I'm not falling for that.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I might as well stand in the middle of the street shouting, "Look at me, I'm an idiot"!

dialogues.speaker: Phonograph
dialogues.text: I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: H—Hey...!? Why's my voice coming from over there?

dialogues.speaker: Oblivious Passerby
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that? You're an idiot? Haha, you can say that again!

dialogues.speaker: Nosy Passerby
dialogues.text: Hello, "An Idiot," nice to meet you! Hahaha! Did you lose a bet or something?

dialogues.speaker: Rational Passerby
dialogues.text: Sounds like a prank to me. Some dumb kid must have got tricked.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Arghhhh! Stop it... NOW!

dialogues.speaker: Phonograph
dialogues.text: I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Calm down, Prune! There's no need for violence...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: A... A... ALICE!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hello, everyone. Well, well, well, I wasn't expecting a challenge like that! It's certainly a novel approach. Anyway, congratulations on successfully activating your Witch's Homework Challenge!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I've prepared a magical space for you with a real sense of pomp and circumstance... But it's going to take a while to load...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: So I thought, why not turn your challenge into loading music while you wait? Play it again and again to really build the excitement and get you properly pumped up. What d'you think?

response.speaker: Phonograph
response.text: I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot! I'm an idiot!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Hey! That wasn't a challenge! Turn that stupid noise off right now!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh dear! It looks like there's been a misunderstanding... I'm afraid the loading music's already merged with the challenge. If I cancel it now, you'll fail the whole thing...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But, I mean, if you're certain. I guess you can try another time, if fate decides we should meet again...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: N—No... Don't you dare run away again! Not after I finally tracked you down. Aaaagh... How much longer does this thing need to load!?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Huh, the magic space? Haha, it loaded ages ago.

talks.objective: Go to the magical simulated space
Go to the magical simulated space

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Welcome to the pinnacle of the dramatic arts in all of Teyvat — the Opera Epiclese... or rather, a magical facsimile of it!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Your challenge is to win a debate, which is exactly why this magical space was created. Not bad, huh? Go on, try telling me the sense of spectacle isn't overwhelming you!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: A debate? Don't you remember how I wiped the floor with you last time? Did you really go to all this trouble just to embarrass yourself again?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehehe... Well done! You displayed the intellect of a 16-year-old in a debate designed for 12-year-olds. How remarkable you are!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I know how much you like to argue, so I've prepared a wonderful topic that even you won't be able to refute!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: A spirited debate requires a fair and impartial judge. Naturally, you were the only candidate worth considering, and I'm sure everyone else here agrees.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then... is Paimon supposed to be up there?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Actually, I've been wanting to say this for ages. Paimon's been sitting up there in the VIP seats striking a pose for quite a while now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... Seeing as we teleported right here, I figured we should imitate our friend. She's quite the superstar in Fontaine, y'know!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: As I recall, Paimon loves watching a good show. Well, there's no better seat in the house, wouldn't you say, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can see everything! But, uhm, is it really alright for Paimon to watch from up here? She feels a little out of place...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Relax. This is my magic space, and I make the rules. I guarantee you the hoi polloi police aren't coming to kick you out.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And then there's Paimon, up there in the box seats. How's the view from up high, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is amazing! Paimon's never sat anywhere this fancy before... She's actually kinda scared to speak, in case someone finds out she's not meant to be here...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Well, you'd better get used to it quick, because we're going to need your cheers and applause in just a moment...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Enough time-wasting. Let's get this over with. What's the topic?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: ...Klee Is a Bad Kid!

response.speaker: Paimon & Prune
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: This is the topic for you to refute. If you can convince our judge that "Klee is not a bad kid," you'll earn yourself a gift.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: I don't want your stupid gift! Klee's your own daughter! How could you set a topic like this?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: You... you're a bad person! The worst person!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hehe... People do say, "Like mother, like daughter." Since I'm so bad, I guess Klee must be pretty bad, too?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Objection! That's pure sophistry. Your flaws lie in your character and conduct — there's no scientific evidence to show that those are hereditary traits.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Nurture has shown a far greater influence than nature. The people who look after Klee in Mondstadt are all better than you. Under their positive influence, Klee couldn't possibly turn out bad!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Do you dispute that Klee loves fish blasting? How could any good kid enjoy such a terrible pastime?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Th—That's just the nature of a child who hasn't been taught right from wrong!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Klee can see the boats in the harbor loaded with fish. How is she supposed to know the difference between how they get their catch and how she gets hers?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But is it not true that even after being sent to solitary confinement, Klee never learns her lesson?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: It's true that Klee always accepts her solitary confinement and doesn't try to escape. That clearly shows she understands her punishment and doesn't hide from her actions.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Klee shouldn't be labelled as bad when she readily faces the consequences of her actions.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Moreover, after her last time in solitary confinement, despite saying she wanted to go fish blasting, she hasn't done it once without permission.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: In fact, the last time she did go, it was only at the behest — you could say instigation — of someone she trusted. Her own mother, no less!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Mm.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: At the end of the day, there's only one person here who deserves the title of "Bad Kid"! No, wait... "Bad Adult"! Hmm... But then what adult is so immature? ...I know, "Bad Kid-ult"!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's what I call a comeback!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, very compelling... A truly forceful argument! How's Alice going to respond?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Even if I accept your argument, it only proves that Klee has no bad intentions. It doesn't stop her from being a bad kid in other people's eyes.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Still stubbornly clinging on...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Fine, if that's your angle, then listen carefully, because here's something even you can't deny...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: "In other people's eyes," Klee is cute, so they will always forgive her actions!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hear, hear!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Klee is so cute, who cares if she makes a few itsy-bitsy mistakes? In Paimon's eyes, she couldn't possibly be bad!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Contrary to everything you've said, Klee has far more good points than bad. She's always happy to share her toys, and when she wants to play but everyone else is busy, she never pesters them, and waits patiently until they're free instead...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: But most important of all, she's kind. In her eyes, everyone is a wonderful person... even me, her mother's sworn enemy...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: No matter what else, I won't let you besmirch such an adorable child by calling her bad!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I give up! You win — as her mother, I can't possibly argue with that, hahaha.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: To hear you say those words... It seems you truly do consider Klee a good friend.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: My daughter really is adorable, isn't she? Don't say I didn't warn you! I told you, if you met her, you'd end up happy.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Now you're boasting? I traveled all the way to Mondstadt because of your silly little prank!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hahaha, it brings me so much comfort knowing that Klee has a friend like you by her side.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I do so look forward to seeing you both grow up. You can't imagine Klee still fish blasting at my age, can you?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Hold it right there... You're not about to say something corny like, "Tada! This was all a test to see how you really feel about Klee," are you?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: You catch on quick! Seeing as you already know the deal, let's jump straight to announcing the results. Esteemed judge, if you will...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem. "Little Prune's Witch Challenge: Passed! Please accept the following Witch's Blessing"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "May you be as happy, healthy, well-fed, and worry-free as Klee herself."

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: When it comes down to it, you and Klee are both good kids. You're allowed to make mistakes from time to time, or even throw cutey-wutey little tantrums, hehe.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Uhm... Thanks? But this doesn't change anything between us. First things first, stop treating me like a child!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: And second things second, I'm a Witch Hunter, and I won't forget my duty! You lost this time, so come out here and stop trying to fool me with that stupid doll.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh me, oh my, would you look at the time? Haha... Well, I had a LOT of fun today. I'll be sure to drop by the next time I'm free. Toodle-oo!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Hey, did you hear me? I haven't finished with you yet! Don't you dare run away...

choices.text: Now I think about it, so is this entire scene!
Am I supposed to be here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, everything just vanished... Classic Alice, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: You wicked witch! Just you wait, I'll get you one day!
